summary: This Dockerfile builds a Docker image based on Node.js 20 running on Alpine Linux. It sets up a working directory, installs dependencies, adds some system tools we'll need at runtime, copies the application code in, and configures the container to start by running npm start.

explanations.3: We're using node:20-alpine as our base image — this is a lightweight version of Node.js 20 built on Alpine Linux, which keeps the image size small.
explanations.5: WORKDIR sets /app as the directory inside the container where all subsequent commands will run — think of it like cd /app.
explanations.9: This upgrades npm to the latest version before we use it to install our app dependencies, ensuring we have all the latest bug fixes and features.
explanations.12: apk is Alpine's package manager (like apt on Ubuntu). We're installing curl, unzip, and libaio system packages that our app needs, with --no-cache keeping the image lean by not storing package manager cache.
explanations.16: CMD specifies the default command to run when the container starts — in this case, npm start will launch our application.
